chapter: Joining Goodman and views on arranging
title: How he came to Broadway
summary: Percy Kaye brought him into shows; he describes the work as bidding for others.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: As long as we're on the subject of Broadway shows, maybe we could just get a few comments from you on

that.
I take it from our talks the
other day that it is not one of your favorite
past times.

No, it is not.
I'm only there because it affords me a living,
and why that should have happened I don't know.
Percy Kaye (phonetic spelling) got me in-
volved in the early sixties, and when the
phone rings, it's usually a Broadway show.
I don't turn them down, I'm
not equipped to turn them down, but it's like
first year harmony. It's doing someone else's
bidding, but not only one person, it's usually
four or five. The result is a hodge podge of
nothing and I have never heard a show yet
that isn't that.
If you have any desire to make
a thing hang together musically, it might at
one point, but it will never wind up being
that. It's always changed, for someone
always has the right to do it.
